Video conferencing is not inherently secure as a form of internet communication, but it can be made significantly more secure through appropriate measures. Official USPTO documentation explicitly states "Recognizing that Internet communications are not secure," applying this characterization directly to video conferencing [d7][d8]. Similarly, a legal disclaimer notes that "the transmission and content of an e-communication cannot be guaranteed to be secure or free of errors or viruses," covering web conferencing [d9]. However, multiple sources explain that security can be achieved: end-to-end encryption, strong passwords, and software updates are key measures [d1][d2], and platforms like Zoho Meeting encrypt audio, video, and screen sharing to protect data in transit [d6]. Critically, as one source notes, "without protection built directly into the service, there won't be any real security in conference calls you make over the web" — meaning layered add-ons alone are insufficient [d5]. Choosing a platform with robust built-in security features such as SSO authentication, end-to-end encryption, and data backups is essential for secure video conferencing [d4].
